---
title: "Labs"
---

Labs referenced by the Pico course. Course-scoped labs live under
`courses/pico/labs/`; reusable labs shared with other courses live under
the repository-root [`labs/`](../../../labs/index.html) directory.

## Referenced labs

- [Hello Pico](../../../labs/hello-pico/) — the introductory lab used from
  [Part 1 · Introduction](../part-1/01-introduction/lab.qmd). Descriptor:
  [`labs/hello-pico/metadata.yaml`](../../../labs/hello-pico/metadata.yaml).
- [Hello Pico Hands (Kubernetes)](../../../labs/hello-pico-hands-kubernetes/) —
  the runnable *Hands* lab used from
  [Part 3 · Hands](../part-3/05-hands/index.qmd): one provider-neutral
  Hands contract, one `KubernetesHands` adapter, one allowlisted
  reversible action confined by a namespaced `Role` and `resourceNames`
  to a Pico-owned `ConfigMap`. Descriptor:
  [`labs/hello-pico-hands-kubernetes/metadata.yaml`](../../../labs/hello-pico-hands-kubernetes/metadata.yaml).
- [Hello Pico Nervous System (MQTT)](../../../labs/hello-pico-nervous-system-mqtt/) —
  the runnable *nervous-system* lab: author one provider-neutral
  Pico message envelope covering the seven message kinds
  (observation, event, command, delegation, result, presence,
  discovery), populate it with one sample per kind, and run a
  deterministic local verifier for envelope shape, stable-vs-transport
  identity, correlation/causation across delegation → result and
  observation → event, authorization context on commands and
  delegations, MQTT topic mapping, and the EMQX adapter description
  marked `optional-not-executed`. No live broker, no credentials, and
  no external SaaS; the Kubernetes-hosted Manifold RuntimeEnvironment
  from [Hello Two Picos](../../../labs/hello-two-picos/) is reused
  unchanged. Descriptor:
  [`labs/hello-pico-nervous-system-mqtt/metadata.yaml`](../../../labs/hello-pico-nervous-system-mqtt/metadata.yaml).

## Authoring course-scoped labs

Course-scoped labs live in this directory and follow the shared lab
template. Reuse a repository-root lab when the same lab is useful for more
than one course.
